outputs.explanation: This is a scatter plot where each of the 141 points already represents an individual sample measurement (rhythmicity index vs. period), not an average. The side histograms show distributions of these same raw values. Scatter plots of individual measurements are exempt from requiring an additional overlay of individual points.

Each marker represents the mean ± s.d. of 6 replicate samples per reporter/cell line (as stated in the caption), but the plot shows only the averaged point with error bars — the underlying individual replicate measurements are not overlaid or otherwise displayed.

These are fitted probability density curves (normal/gamma distributions) illustrating the spread of subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes. Line/density plots of this kind are exempt from requiring individual point overlays.

Box plots inherently display the data distribution (quartiles, median, whiskers) and are exempt from the individual-data-point requirement; the image additionally overlays individual sample dots, further supporting a pass.

Polar histograms display frequency/probability distributions of phase differences over time; histogram-type plots inherently convey distribution shape and are not required to overlay additional individual points.
Same rationale as panel E: a polar histogram showing distribution of phase differences averaged by subtype; histogram plots are exempt from requiring individual point overlays.

This is a line plot of a single example signal with its fitted model and decay envelope, illustrating a method rather than presenting averaged data across replicates; line plots are exempt from the individual-point requirement.

This is a scatter plot where each of the 117 points represents an individual sample's fitted amplitude and decay rate; the error bars reflect fitting uncertainty for that single sample rather than variability across averaged replicates, so the points themselves are the individual data.
